the ML based CAD diagnosis studies published between 1998 and 2019 are not comparable, as they are based on datasets with different sample sizes and features, and that the ML techniques applied in the studies are not comparable, because the performance metrics are different and the datasets are not the same.

(1) ML based CAD diagnosis is a challenging and promising task, (2) the performance of the ML techniques depends on the dataset and applied ML techniques, and (3) there are still important challenges and shortcomings that need to be addressed in order to make ML based CAD diagnosis more effective.

the results that have been reported on ML based CAD detection are not comparable.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ML based CAD diagnosis can be improved by using larger and balanced datasets, by considering the stenosis levels of each coronary artery, by employing more advanced ML techniques, and by developing a more reliable CAD dataset.

ML based CAD diagnosis can be improved by increasing the sample size and the number of features, using the stenosis values of the coronary arteries in the dataset, using the ML technique with feature selection, and employing performance metrics that are more sensitive to CAD diagnosis.
ML based CAD diagnosis is a fast, noninvasive, and affordable alternative to angiography, but it is still in its infancy and requires more research to be widely accepted by the medical community.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of ML based CAD detection methods is strongly affected by the dataset characteristics and the applied techniques.
there is no one-size-fits-all solution for CAD diagnosis, and the results of the literature cannot be compared.
there is a need to standardize the data collection, feature selection, and ML methods to enable a more reliable and accurate diagnosis of CAD.
